newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Kasich hints might enter White House race.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Kasich hints might enter White House race.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich, briefly mentioned as a possible running mate of Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole last year, hinted Wednesday he might run for the top office.
The 44-year-old Ohio Republican, who has been somewhat of a maverick in the House leadership, said his decision would depend on how effective he believes the political leaders are at the time.
But he did not say whether he would be judging the strength of the Republican field or the Democratic opposition, which is assumed to be Vice President Al Gore for the 2000 election.

"I am going to take a look at who's got the ball in their hands. If people who have the ball in their hands can really slam dunk then I don't need to do it. But if they are not getting the job done then I am going to have to step up and do it," he said, when asked by a member of the Independent Insurance Agents whether he would run for president.
"If I played for the Chicago Bulls I would not try to dunk the ball, I would let Michael Jordan do it," he said in remarks to the agents after a speech at a local hotel.

Kasich leads the House negotiations on reaching a balanced budget with the White House. In addition to reducing taxes, Kasich has as a key issue the reform of what he has termed "corporate welfare," government subsidies for business.
